title: Serious adverse event: late neurotropic disease associated with yellow fever vaccine.
ehr_evidence: Clinical case report of a 9-month-old infant at Hospital Geral de Carapicuíba, with data from physical examination, laboratory tests, computed tomography, and vaccination records.
summary: Case report of a previously healthy 9-month-old infant who developed late neurotropic disease 20 days after yellow fever vaccination, presenting with fever, strabismus, cervical muscle weakness, and leg weakness, followed by complete recovery after supportive care.
key_findings: Positive IgM for yellow fever virus in cerebrospinal fluid confirmed vaccine-associated neurotropic disease (N=1).
Patient showed clinical improvement by day 5 and complete recovery by day 10.
Tests for bacteria and herpes-virus were negative.
captured_features: laboratory tests (CSF, blood biochemistry, leukogram, liver/renal function, CRP)
population: 9-month-old male infant, previously healthy, from São Paulo, Brazil
